note: Row ids mirror manifests/spec.json: '1'..'8' are the numbered '### N.' parameter sections of the spec; 'arch-logic-tile', 'arch-routing' and 'arch-bitstream' are the three inherited architectural rows, which the spec does not number, so ids were assigned here. No spec row is edited.

rows.reason: Structural: the cell set (4x LUT4 plus one output FF per LUT) is fixed by the vendored RTL; it is checked by bitstream-level simulation, not sampled.
Structural: 4 tracks per edge is a netlist property of the switch matrix; routability is a pass/fail routing and DRC result on the layout.
Functional: the bitstream format is generated and checked by bitstream-level tests on the simulated fabric; there is no random variable.
Library and track height are a design choice fixed per tile; whether cells are from the chosen library is a netlist check.
Supply flavour selects the nominal corner only; the timing claim is bounded by the shipped liberty corners (row 5), not by a distribution.
Metal-stack option and layer budget are fixed by the tech LEF; per-layer utilization is a measured layout result and routing closure is pass/fail.
Area, utilization and aspect ratio are measured results of one placed-and-routed layout; no statistical ceiling is ratified.
Timing is corner-bounded: STA must be clean at every shipped liberty corner of the chosen library, so the claim is a worst-case bound, not a sigma or yield figure.
Corners are the enumerated, shipped liberty set (15 per library); they are a finite list to be run, not a sampled distribution.
Fabric size is a structural choice (2x2 to 4x4 of one tile) validated by assembly and abutment checks.
Signoff is DRC and LVS pass/fail on the final GDS, with ERC and antenna reported; no mismatch or Monte Carlo analysis is claimed.
